title: Alcohol, Cannabis and Nicotine: How They Can Affect Mental Health and Psychiatric Medications
description: Because substances can change sleep, mood, anxiety, attention, cardiovascular effects, withdrawal symptoms, medication tolerability, and safety. Accurate information supports safer prescribing; the purpose is better clinical information, not judgment.

references.title: SAMHSA — Substance Use Disorder Treatment Options

body:
No Judgment\. Just Better Information\.

Alcohol\, cannabis\, nicotine\, prescription medications\, and other substances can affect mood\, anxiety\, attention\, sleep\, motivation\, heart rate\, blood pressure\, and how medications feel or work\.

That\'s why we\'ll ask about them\.

Not to judge you\.

Not to get you in trouble\.

We need an accurate picture of everything your brain and body are being exposed to so we can make safer\, better\-informed treatment decisions\.

## Why It Matters

A substance may seem to help one symptom in the short term while making another problem worse later\.

For example\:

Alcohol may make you sleepy but disrupt sleep later in the night\. → Nicotine may briefly improve alertness but withdrawal between doses can contribute to → irritability\, anxiety\, or difficulty concentrating\.

Cannabis may feel relaxing but for some people it can worsen anxiety\, memory\, → motivation\, attention\, or psychiatric symptoms\.

Stimulant or recreational substances may increase energy while also affecting sleep\, → anxiety\, heart rate\, and blood pressure\.

This doesn\'t mean every person responds the same way\.

That\'s exactly why we ask\.

Alcohol

Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant\, even though some people initially feel more social\, relaxed\, or energized after drinking\.

Alcohol can affect\:

Sleep • Mood • Anxiety • Judgment • Coordination • Memory • Impulse control

It can also interact with psychiatric medications\.

Combining alcohol with medications or substances that cause sedation can be particularly risky\.

If alcohol is part of your life\, tell us how much and how often rather than simply saying \"occasionally\.\"

That information helps\.

Cannabis

People use cannabis for many reasons\:

Sleep • Anxiety • Pain • Relaxation • Appetite • Recreation • Trauma symptoms

Some people perceive benefits\.

Others experience\:

Anxiety • Panic • Paranoia • Memory problems • Reduced concentration • Changes in

motivation • Sleep problems

Cannabis products also vary substantially in THC concentration\, formulation\, and frequency of use\, so \"I use marijuana\" doesn\'t tell us everything we need to know\.

If you use cannabis\, we\'d rather know\.

## Nicotine \& Vaping

Nicotine is a stimulant and is highly reinforcing\.

It can temporarily affect\:

Alertness • Attention • Mood • Heart rate • Blood pressure

When nicotine levels fall\, withdrawal can cause\:

Irritability • Restlessness • Anxiety • Difficulty concentrating • Cravings

That can create an important clinical question\:

\"Is my ADHD\/anxiety getting worse—or am I experiencing nicotine withdrawal\?\"

Sometimes it\'s both\.

Vapes and nicotine pouches can also make it surprisingly easy to consume nicotine repeatedly throughout the day\.

## Prescription Medications Can Matter Too

Taking a medication exactly as prescribed is different from misusing it—but we still need the full picture\.

Tell us about medications including\:

Pain medications • Benzodiazepines • Sleep medications • Stimulants • Muscle relaxants •

Weight\-loss medications • Other controlled medications

Also tell us about medications prescribed by other providers\.

Your psychiatric medication doesn\'t exist in isolation from everything else you\'re taking\.

## Other Substances

Please tell us about other substances too\, including things that may feel uncomfortable to discuss\.

Our priority is safety and effective treatment\.

Knowing about substance use can change decisions involving\:

Medication selection • Dosing • Drug interactions • Withdrawal risk • Overdose risk •

Cardiovascular monitoring • Sleep treatment • ADHD treatment

Accurate information helps us protect you\.

## Mixing Substances Can Change the Risk

One substance may be relatively predictable by itself but become substantially more dangerous when combined with another\.

Of particular concern is combining multiple substances or medications that slow the central nervous system and breathing\.

If you\'re unsure whether something you\'re taking is safe with your medication\, ask\.

That\'s a good question—not an inconvenience\.

## Recovery Isn\'t All\-or\-Nothing

If you\'re trying to reduce or stop substance use\, progress may not follow a perfectly straight line\.

A return to use doesn\'t erase everything you\'ve learned\.

Instead ask\:

What happened before it\?

What was I feeling\?

Who was I with\?

What need was I trying to meet\?

What could make the next situation safer\?

Understanding the pattern gives us something to work with\.

## Be Curious About the Job the Substance Is Doing

Instead of only asking\:

\"How do I stop\?\"

also ask\:

\"What is this doing for me\?\"

Maybe it helps you\:

Fall asleep \* Feel less anxious

Concentrate \* Feel confident socially

Escape painful emotions \* Have energy

Feel less bored \* Manage pain

Feel something \* Feel nothing

Connect with other people

If we understand the function\, we can work on finding safer ways to meet the same need\.

## Try One Experiment

You don\'t necessarily have to promise\:

\"I\'m never doing this again\.\"

Start by collecting information\.

For one week\, notice\:

What did I use\?

How much\?

What time\?

What was happening immediately beforehand\?

How did I feel afterward\?

How did I sleep\?

How did I feel the next day\?

What did I learn\?

## Recovery Support Is Available

You don\'t have to make changes alone\.

Support can include\:

Individual treatment • Therapy • Peer recovery support • USARA • SMART Recovery • AA •

NA • The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter\-day Saints Addiction Recovery Program \(ARP\) •

Family\/community support

There are multiple pathways to recovery\.

We can help you explore options that fit your individual needs\, goals\, and values\.

## The Ischys Takeaway

We\'re not asking\:

\"Are you being good or bad\?\"

We\'re asking\:

\"What is going into your brain and body\, what is it doing for you\, and is it helping you get where you want to go\?\"

You can talk with us about substance use\.

Honest information helps us provide safer care\.

## Notice Understand Experiment Track Discuss → → → →

This information is for general education and does not replace individualized medical or substance\-use treatment\. Abruptly stopping some substances—including heavy alcohol use\, benzodiazepines\, and certain medications—can cause dangerous withdrawal\. Talk with a healthcare professional before abruptly stopping a substance when physical dependence may be present\.
